blocks.text: Elkanah’s yearly journey to Shiloh places Hannah’s prayer and Samuel’s dedication at a named regional gathering place. Judges also associates Shiloh with the house of God and an annual festival of YHWH, helping explain why this location frames the family’s repeated worship in the chapter.

Archaeological evidence documents occupation at Shiloh, but it does not identify the installations or annual event described in the narratives. The place can therefore be understood as a named gathering location without treating its remains as proof of the specific sanctuary setting or festival.

sections.title: What the evidence can and cannot show

blocks.text: This opening chapter begins the book’s movement from Eli’s failing priestly house through Samuel’s prophetic leadership, Saul’s rejected kingship, and David’s anointing, rise, exile, and Saul’s death.
